A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Universal Sequence Preconditioning by the same authors. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on synthetic linear, nonlinear, and RNN-generated sequences and ETTh1, with results in Tables 2–4 and Figures 1 and 3–5.

after.justification: v5 retains these original synthetic and ETTh1 experiments, including numerical results and appendix plots.

M1.justification: The spectral-filtering procedure changes substantially. v5 weights the spectral feature vector by (1−α²), changing the covariance matrix and filter basis. Algorithm 3 also replaces p_n(x) with (1−x²)p_n(x) and extends its target-history term from n to n+2 coefficients. Algorithms 1, 2, and 4 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear dynamical systems, nonlinear systems, deep-RNN-generated sequences, and ETTh1 task. The revised theoretical eigenvalue restrictions do not introduce an additional empirical scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparisons: no preconditioning, Chebyshev coefficients, Legendre coefficients, and jointly learned coefficients within the reported regression, spectral-filtering, and DNN experiments.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same sequence lengths, predictor dimensions, learning-rate searches, polynomial degrees, and final-200-prediction absolute-error metric. ETTh1 retains the 5000-step horizon and Adam setup. No experimental protocol revision is reported alongside the Algorithm 3 changes.

E4.justification: The polynomial-degree and complex-threshold sensitivity analyses are retained, including the learned-coefficient instability findings. Figures 3–5 and their accompanying discussion move from v3 Appendix G to v5's final Appendix C without new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean±standard deviation across 200 synthetic runs and average the ETTh1 results over 10 independent runs. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain identical numerical entries, and the empirical plots are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains baseline error 0.54±0.23 and degree-5 Chebyshev error 0.08±0.03. The formal regret-bound revisions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.2 changes from average error O-tilde(T^−3/13) under an inverse-log-squared eigenvalue-argument restriction to O-tilde(T^−1/39) under |arg(λ)|≤T^−1/3. Appendix E replaces the exponential spectral-decay proof using quadrature and Zolotarev arguments with trace-based bounds, revises the approximation and regret theorems, and introduces a parameterized rate tradeoff. A new Lemma A.1 analyzes kernel norms; the regression and Chebyshev proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1, and Discussion retain the same headline contributions and empirical claims. Section 1.1 still claims O-tilde(T^−3/13) spectral-filtering regret; it is not updated to reflect the weaker revised Theorem 2.2. Changing 'input' to 'target' in the abstract clarifies the already-described operation.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly calls Theorem 2.2 weak, emphasizes its polynomially small eigenvalue-argument requirement, and states that the proof relies mainly on preconditioning rather than critical spectral-filtering properties. Section 2.2 defers deeper spectral analysis to future work. These substantially qualify the mechanism and applicability, although Section 3 retains the older stronger explanation.

D1.justification: The experimental data-generation instructions, model dimensions, optimizer information, and tuning grids are retained. No implementation, hardware, timing, or code/data-access information is added or removed; revised mathematical parameter conditions are covered under M1 and T1.

R1.justification: Four mathematical references supporting the discarded proof are removed: Ahlfors, Dimitrov and Nikolov, Knight and Newbery, and Stoer and colleagues. The novel spectral-decay proof is recast as a standard eigenvalue bound, while the broader related-work discussion and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 corrects abstract terminology, consolidates paragraphs, adds acknowledgements, and reorganizes Appendix E into preliminaries and result subsections. The overall narrative remains recognizable. Final appendices are relabeled, introducing duplicate A, B, and C appendix identifiers.

P2.justification: The same four tables and five figures are retained. Figure 1 moves onto the page containing Tables 2–4, and Figure 2 moves within its proof. Text and algorithm floats reflow, while the contents list spills onto a nearly empty second page. The displays are not substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: The explicit caution about spectral filtering is useful, but v5 leaves Sections 1.1 and 3 asserting the old T^−3/13 advantage while Theorem 2.2 now states T^−1/39 under a stricter condition. Its new Lemma A.1 also analyzes a squared (1−α²) factor although Equation 4 defines a single factor. These unreconciled claims and definitions reduce internal reliability; the retained empirical evaluation provides no corresponding quality change.
